subject: Media Literacy
title: Reporters and Their Sources
description: A short lesson to help you apply Reporters and Their Sources.

hook.text: Watergate was broken by two reporters and one anonymous source called 'Deep Throat.'

buildup.text: Journalists rely on sources — officials, witnesses, experts, and documents — to construct stories.

discovery.text: Anonymous sources protect whistleblowers but also allow officials to float ideas without accountability.

twist.text: When you read 'sources say,' ask: who benefits from this information being published right now?

climax.text: Sources aren't neutral. Everyone who talks to a reporter has a reason for talking.

punchline.text: Every source has a motive. Every quote has a purpose.

quiz.question: What should you ask when a news story cites anonymous sources?
options: Who benefits from this information being published?
